description: Sighting a humpback whale from a boat can be awe-inspiring. For some BC Ferries passengers, that experience became disturbing when their ferry struck and fatally injured a humpback whale on Oct. 18.
title: Mourning Notcho: What one whale's death teaches us about ecological grief

description: Water flooded the pasture, spilling from an irrigation pipe tucked alongside a hill at the Sierra Foothill Research and Extension Center, a University of California research facility located about 20 miles (32 kilometers) east of Yuba City. For more than three hours, starting at 6 a.m. this summer day, the water had seeped into the soils beneath the yellow-green grass, spreading to various depths while flowing downslope toward its destination.
title: How enhanced rock weathering can speed up carbon capture

description: Social media offers everyone the same basic promise: post something about yourself and get responses from other people. Whether it's a vacation, a promotion or just a midweek meal, these days many people's lives are shared online.
title: Could your personality be affecting how you feel about social media?

description: SpaceX brought back its Starship rocket's second stage today for a first-ever midair capture at its launch pad, capping a record-setting orbital flight test.
title: Baby, she's back: SpaceX catches a Starship from orbit for first time

description: For centuries, optical systems have relied on lenses, mirrors and other components that manipulate light through their shape and size. Today, advances in nanotechnology are enabling a different approach. Researchers can now engineer materials at scales smaller than the wavelength of light, creating ultrathin optical components that offer new ways to control how light behaves.
title: Flat optics roadmap charts path toward smaller imaging and sensing systems

description: When the universe was less than 700 million years old, the supermassive black hole powering a quasar called J0313-1806 had already grown to about 3 billion times the mass of the sun. It is one of the most extreme examples of a puzzle that has occupied astrophysicists for two decades: How did supermassive black holes grow so big so quickly?
title: Early black holes may have grown through productive chaos

description: Nearly every person will run into conflict in their workplace at some point in their career, but it can be difficult to know when or how to report these concerns.
title: 'Buffer spaces' may help resolve workplace concerns

description: Artificial intelligence programs could be used to improve efficiency for professionals dealing with research ethics reviews, enabling humans to focus on the ethical decision-making.
title: AI could help speed up research ethics approvals

description: Stacking chips on top of one another could keep computers getting faster, but it creates a heating problem. Now, researchers from Japan have found that simply flipping atom-thin layers upside down could help steer that heat where it needs to go.
title: Flip side: Upside-down atomic layers could steer heat in stacked computer chips

description: As early as 130,000 years ago, the first human societies were built on morality and cooperation within groups. The same is true today. Even young children exhibit a distinctly human desire to be seen as morally good. That is the conclusion of a new article by researchers at Leipzig University. Humboldt Research Fellow Dr. Leon Li and Junior Professor Dr. Sebastian Grüneisen are investigating the origins of human cooperation and social identity. Their paper, "Evolutionary foundations of social identity," has just been published in the journal Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.
title: New analysis shows that even young children want to be seen as morally good

description: Forget about how the zebra got its stripes. For a group of Cornell engineers, an equally important question is: What drives the formation of such eye-catching patterns?
title: Tigers, zebras, quantum dots: Nanoparticles assemble into patterns

description: A UCLA-developed technology that is like a test tube but on the cellular scale has led to a number of biomedical discoveries in recent years, including revelations about cancer, heart disease and the genetic levers that push cells to release proteins.
title: Capping nanovials that trap cells and their secretions for analysis enables new bioscience experiments

description: Majdi Abou Najm stands in a tomato crop under the summer sun in UC Davis' agricultural research fields. A few hours after sunrise, the sun is beginning to feel less like warmth and more like a weight—the kind of heat that could scald tomatoes on the vine.
title: Researchers are testing whether agrivoltaics can help farmers adapt to hotter, drier conditions

description: Euclid was launched into space in July 2023 to explore two of astronomy's biggest mysteries: dark matter and dark energy. The space telescope's first major data release covers some 1,900 square degrees of the sky, equivalent to around 14% of the area planned for the six-year mission and around 5% of the total sky. It is an unprecedented collection of visible and near-infrared observations.
title: Euclid's H-alpha observations map where stars form in distant galaxies

description: As the demand for sustainable alternatives to conventional plastics continues to grow, biodegradable polymers such as poly(lactic acid) (PLA) are attracting increasing attention for applications ranging from packaging to consumer products.
title: Long-term study reveals how humidity affects the durability of biodegradable thermoplastic polymers

description: From light switches to transistors, many kinds of switches have exactly two states: on or off, conducting or insulating, zero or one. Researchers at TU Wien are working with unusual materials that challenge some of the standard assumptions of materials physics. Using one of these materials, they have developed a tiny switch with four distinct states and several ways to move between them. This opens up new ways to process and store information. The study is published in the journal Communications Materials.
title: Tiny switch harnesses four electrical states, moving beyond simple on-off control

description: Texas A&M University researchers have developed a process that converts biomass into renewable fuels and chemicals. Dr. Mark Holtzapple, professor in the Artie McFerrin Department of Chemical Engineering, aims to make producing these products more efficient and affordable by using microorganisms to break down plant material.
title: Turning biomass into renewable fuels and chemicals using microorganisms

description: Your mission, should you choose to accept it: Track down and identify thousands of nearly microscopic mosquito eggs hiding in plain sight. Your only weapon? A smartphone armed with artificial intelligence.
title: AI tool counts mosquito eggs in smartphone photos to aid surveillance

description: Using high-resolution observations from the New Vacuum Solar Telescope (NVST), a research team from the Yunnan Observatories of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) has systematically studied the kinematic properties of dynamic fibrils around a sunspot and the mechanisms that drive them. The study was published in The Astrophysical Journal on Nov. 10.
title: Sunspot dynamic fibrils linked to slow magnetoacoustic waves

description: Researchers from the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST) have created a spin-based microwave amplifier that operates near absolute zero, boosting signals by more than 1,000-fold while adding noise close to the bare minimum required by the laws of physics. As a more robust alternative to current state-of-the-art devices, the OIST device can handle much stronger signals and operate in magnetic fields, paving the way for practical quantum computing and higher-resolution sensing technologies.
title: Ultracold diamond microwave laser amplifies quantum signals 1,000-fold

description: The ocean is changing rapidly. Warming, acidification, oxygen loss, sea-level rise and the intensification of extreme events are transforming marine ecosystems, leading to species shifts and mass mortality events. However, these impacts are not distributed evenly. There are areas that buffer these effects and act as true "marine climate refugia."
title: Why marine climate refugia matter for safeguarding the world's oceans

description: Observations by a team of researchers from Tel Aviv University at the Ramat Gan Safari reveal recurring cooperation between two adult female gorillas, who assume complementary roles to solve a practical problem.
title: Two gorillas form a 'living ladder' to reach high branches

description: Blue eyes in cats have long attracted attention, especially when they occur in cats with fully colored coats. The dominant blue eye (DBE) phenotype has become increasingly visible across several breeds. When we prepared our literature review, four independent DBE variants had been described in scientific publications. Today, eight variants are reported, although published genetic evidence is available for six. Some of these variants are also associated with health concerns.
title: The expanding genetics of blue eyes in cats

description: Colleges use AI tools for academic advising, analyzing data to predict which students need additional help. But research from Princeton Engineering suggests that helping students requires judgment and expertise that go beyond the algorithm.
title: Can AI replace college advisers? Research says not yet

description: Developing countries hardest hit by climate change were promised a new source of support when governments agreed at the annual global climate change conference in 2022 (COP27) to create a Loss and Damage fund. This fund was intended to help them cope with losses ranging from destroyed homes and livelihoods to the loss of lives and cultural heritage.
title: COP 31: Who qualifies for loss and damage funding? Why country borders are a poor guide

description: Donna dePolo and Shijie Zhong have never set foot on Antarctica. But with the help of satellites measuring ground motions and gravity, a supercomputer in Wyoming and years of seismic data collected at remote Antarctic research stations, the CU Boulder physicists have created a detailed picture of what's been happening beneath the West Antarctic ice as it rapidly melts.
title: 3D model generates most detailed picture yet of what's going on beneath West Antarctica's melting ice

description: Delegates from around the world are currently gathering in Antalya, Turkey, for COP31. Among the issues up for discussion will be an important question: Who should pay for the harms caused by climate change?
title: Universities should follow communities' lead on climate research

description: Researchers at the UCLA Samueli School of Engineering and Auburn University have achieved a scientific first: They measured atomic vibrations that carry heat and sound waves, and connected them to a quantum property called spin, which is a way of characterizing a subatomic particle's built-in magnetism.
title: Measurements reveal link between quantum spin and sound-carrying vibrations in an ultrathin semiconductor

description: South Africa is entering a potentially difficult summer for farmers. El Niño is already established: the warming of the Pacific Ocean's surface that affects weather patterns globally and brings about severe weather phenomena like floods, droughts and heat waves. The World Meteorological Organisation expects it to strengthen into a very strong event toward the end of 2026, with effects likely to continue into early 2027.
title: Super El Niño could leave South Africa short of grazing. Timing of livestock fodder crops is crucial

description: The oldest evidence of domesticated corn dates back more than 9,000 years and was found in the lowlands of the Balsas River Valley in southwest Mexico. Around that time, nomadic hunter-gatherers began selecting, collecting and planting seeds from desirable versions of an annual grass now known as teosinte.
title: Wet climate may have helped corn reach Mexican highlands and crossbreed with wild grass

description: By now, almost everyone has asked an AI agent a question, only to realize that the answer seems not quite right. Something might be missing or wrong or out of date. An executive assistant told me she uses AI tools for drafting itineraries and briefings, but she's caught enough issues that she now builds time into her workflow to thoroughly check for inaccuracies and biases.
title: Catching AI's mistakes is a mental burden—and a drag on productivity

description: Antiferromagnets are regarded as important materials for next-generation electronics. It is difficult, however, to accurately measure some of their properties. A new study by a team of researchers from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (MLU) and the Max Planck Institute for Microstructure Physics, working as part of the Cluster of Excellence Center for Chiral Electronics, explains why this is the case.
title: Chiral electronics: Researchers discover a disruptive interlayer in a promising material system

description: LMP1 is an Epstein-Barr virus protein that has a "Mr. Hyde" side that can promote cancer and a "Dr. Jekyll" side that can spur antitumor immune responses. Scientists at Hiroshima University have now traced key antitumor immune effects of LMP1 to two transcription factors, Spi-B and IRF1, and found that expressing the two together made tumor cells easier for the immune system to recognize and better able to activate CD8+ T cells without using the viral protein itself.
title: Two transcription factors reproduce the beneficial side of a 'Jekyll and Hyde' viral protein

description: Water is vital to life, which is part of why we study what's in it.
title: Annual water‑quality reports don't tell the full story of what you're drinking

description: Researchers led by professor Zeng Fanjiang and associate professor Gao Yanju from the Xinjiang Institute of Ecology and Geography of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (XIEG) have revealed the contrasting yet complementary roles of plant roots and mycorrhizal mycelia in shaping soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics during hyper-arid afforestation. Their study was published in New Phytologist on Nov. 4.
title: Root and mycelium pathways shape soil carbon dynamics in hyper-arid regions

description: Two airborne pollutants are turning up together more often in the contiguous U.S. as wildfires grow larger, a shift that exacerbates health hazards, according to a research team in the Penn State College of Earth and Mineral Sciences.
title: Combined pollutants from wildfire smoke exacerbate health risks across US

description: New research from the University of Tübingen and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology in Jena gives valuable clues as to economic development in various regions across thousands of years. Researchers evaluated 18,457 skeletal remains and analyzed changes in height, estimated from thighbone length. The bones come from 45 different countries across Europe and Asia. The study has been published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
title: Ancient height trends show technological advances did not always improve living standards

description: Stanford University researchers have shown that the median sand grain size in dunes on Earth and Mars reveals the speed of the winds that formed those dunes. The finding enables scientists to use sand as a wind speedometer for both modern and ancient dunes found across the solar system.
title: Written in sand: How dunes reveal the secrets of planetary winds

description: A woodcock is an odd little bird with a long, skinny bill and a plump, chunky body that's shaped like an American football. It mostly hangs out near the ground, but it does a mating display in which it makes a buzzy, tweeting call and then takes off zigzagging across the sky. The woodcock stands out from most of the members of its family, the sandpipers. The majority of sandpiper species are champion migrators that traverse thousands of miles every year, but many woodcock species and their closest cousins, the snipes, have evolved to migrate shorter distances. Some island-dwelling species of woodcocks and snipes don't migrate at all.
title: How woodcocks evolved to be the weird cousins of their family

description: The first few notes of an electric guitar can send memories from your teenage years rushing back. These memories often feel intensely personal. But a new study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences finds that the memories evoked by songs are surprisingly similar from person to person and vary with a song's genre and decade.
title: Songs from same genre or era evoke similar memories across listeners

description: Humanity is quickly reaching the limits of our ability to track all the satellites we have in deep space. NASA's Deep Space Network (DSN) has been the workhorse for tracking them for decades but is quickly being overwhelmed by the number of requests it receives, which in turn makes it harder to track some recently launched missions.
title: Navigating lunar orbit using nothing but shadows and a power meter

description: More than 100 million severe infections are believed to be caused worldwide each year by various species of amoebae, single-celled organisms typically found in freshwater and saltwater and moist environments. While treatment with antibiotics for these infections is often effective, scientists have long believed the body's own immune cells were unable to defend against amoebae.
title: New study reveals immune cells' ability to engulf and destroy amoebae

description: A Korean research team has identified how impurities interfere with the use of waste plastic pyrolysis oil as a petrochemical feedstock through catalytic experiments and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational chemistry. The findings, published in the journal ACS Catalysis, provide a scientific basis for predicting potential declines in catalytic performance according to the types and concentrations of impurities present.
title: AI and experiments reveal impurities hindering waste plastic pyrolysis oil recycling

description: Ukraine recently captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war. According to the Ukrainian state-run I Want to Live project, the 49-year-old man from Java had been promised work in Russia's construction industry only to realize he had been recruited into the army while being transported to Donetsk.
title: 'Forced fighters' are being lured into Ukraine war under false pretenses

description: An international research team, led by scientists from Skoltech, has experimentally demonstrated for the first time the photonic spin Hall shift for light scattered off an optically small particle. This work, published in the Advanced Photonics journal, overcomes a long-standing challenge in optics and could contribute to the development of next-generation optical technologies, advanced radar and lidar systems.
title: Elusive optical effect paves the way for advanced lidar and nanophotonic technologies

description: A new study shows that understanding decisions made by juries requires attention not only to their final verdicts but also to how jurors make decisions individually and work together to reach a verdict, especially when they disagree. Led by Tova Cohen, a Ph.D. student at Rutgers School of Criminal Justice, the research studied 35 participants in seven virtual mock juries to examine individuals' characteristics, deliberative participation, changed verdicts and dissent.
title: Study of juries' decision-making addresses disagreement among jurors

description: The Collins English Dictionary has selected "mogging" as its 2026 word of the year.
title: Mogging is the word of the year—but men have been doing it since Shakespearean times

description: Beneath the North Atlantic Ocean lies a series of underwater volcanic mountain chains stretching from the coast of North America toward the Azores. These include the New England Seamounts and the Great Meteor Seamounts.
title: One wandering plume may have created several Atlantic volcanic chains

description: The population of one of the world's rarest whales has fallen after trending upward in recent years, worrying scientists who fear the animal could still be at risk of extinction.
title: Rare North Atlantic right whale population drops, alarming scientists

description: Every year, around 3.5 billion birds migrate to North America to breed, finding safe havens and nesting grounds in our national parks along the way.
title: Protecting forests outside parks benefits the birds within

description: A country crow hesitates upon seeing a takeout food box. A city crow pauses the first time it sees an ear of corn. Both are taken aback when they find a strange wooden object next to the expected peanuts.
title: City crows and country crows don't see the world the same way

description: Harnessing satellite imagery, AI deep-learning models and community science data, scientists from the University of Minnesota have tracked the spread of leafy spurge over a 20-year period.
title: From 400 miles above Earth, AI tracks invasive leafy spurge

description: We know quite a lot about ancient Mesopotamia, the historical region spanning modern-day Iraq and parts of Syria and Turkey, such as who ruled and the order in which kings succeeded one another. But pinning down exact calendar dates for historical events has been trickier.
title: Ancient tree rings and ice cores help pin down when Babylonia fell

description: When governments have attempted to address environmental problems in recent decades, they have often simply shifted the problem elsewhere or created a new problem for others. A University of Kansas law professor is among a group of scholars who published a study pointing out such environmental problem shifting and proposing "strange loop ethics" as a method to rethink critical legal issues.
title: New ethical approach to environmental issues would avoid 'problem shifting,' law scholar says

description: Firefighting aircraft, helicopters, fire departments—when forests across Europe are burning at the same time, the limited firefighting resources have to be allocated efficiently, and ideally before the fires even break out.
title: Why forest fires often break out simultaneously across Europe

description: From helping fellow tourists find their way to recommending independent shops and local businesses, visitors can play a part in supporting rural communities. New research suggests that the way destinations communicate their social values could encourage more support.
title: Giving an insider's perspective could help rural destinations attract more support from tourists

description: A highly lethal pathogen is responsible for the mass death of tadpoles and the rapid decline of amphibian populations in the Atlantic Forest. A group of researchers demonstrate for the first time in South America that recurring ranavirus outbreaks caused an 83% drop in monkey frog (Phyllomedusa distincta) reproduction in a pond in the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina. The disease is caused by a virus that affects reptiles and fish as well.
title: Deadly virus reduces tree frog population by 83% in Atlantic Forest reserve

description: Fans of Thanksgiving look forward each year to family traditions and a table full of holiday dishes. Less anticipated is the aftermath: cleaning up and deciding what to do with all those leftovers.
title: Q&A: How can consumers reduce food waste around the holidays?

description: In a recent study of infrared light collected by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), a group of astronomers detected ice for the first time around the young star Beta Pictoris. Researchers had expected ice around Beta Pictoris, but previous searches had not directly detected it. The study, published in Science, found that the ice is mostly noncrystalline and mixed with carbon dioxide. The team says these new details provide clues about the early formation of the Beta Pictoris system and collisions that may still be occurring.
title: Dirty ice around young star Beta Pictoris suggests frequent collisions and sheds light on the system's formation

description: Dr. Miguel Bravo-Haro participated in an international study that has reconstructed, for the first time, the ground motion that struck Caraballeda, La Guaira state, Venezuela, during the magnitude 7.5 earthquake of June 24 this year.
title: Reconstructing ground shaking that brought down buildings in Venezuela's earthquake

description: Neodymium–iron–boron (Nd–Fe–B) permanent magnets are key components in electric vehicle traction motors and wind turbines. In particular, heavy rare-earth elements, which are added to maintain coercivity (resistance to demagnetization) even at high temperatures, are extremely expensive and have unstable supply chains, consequently placing a significant burden on industry. Since completely eliminating heavy rare-earth elements remains difficult, the most important technical challenge is to minimize their use while maintaining magnetic performance.
title: Team maximizes efficiency of heavy rare-earth elements for high-performance permanent magnets

description: The slow-moving lava of an effusive volcanic eruption can transform a landscape. But escaping gases, cloud cover, accessibility issues and limited local resources can make monitoring the development of a flow field dangerous and difficult.
title: Satellite radar tracks lava flows and crater changes at Hawaii's Kilauea volcano

description: The annual cycle of Finland's groundwater has changed over the past 50 years, shows a long-term study by the University of Oulu and the Finnish Environment Institute. The findings provide a valuable reference point for examining groundwater change in other northern regions: shallow, fast-responding aquifers occur worldwide. The paper is published in the Journal of Hydrology.
title: Groundwater's annual cycle is shifting: 50-year study in Finland reveals contrasting outcomes in the north and south

description: A pair of researchers has created a new model for radioactive decay, which allows alpha and beta decay to happen simultaneously in a single transition. Testing their model's predictions against a full chart of known isotopes, Wenqiang Zhang at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, together with Chong Qi at the Alba Nova University Centre, Stockholm, showed that these simultaneous emissions could better explain the observed emission spectra of several radioactive isotopes.
title: Model of 'alpha-beta decay' could solve a decades-old nuclear mystery

description: Recently an artificial intelligence proved an 18-year-old conjecture in computer science, called the Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture. The proof settles a long-standing conjecture (educated guess) that eliminates one proposed route to enormous quantum computer speedups, ruling out one particular variant of "quantum supremacy," the term for the hypothesis that a programmable quantum computer can solve a problem that no classical computer can solve in any "feasible" amount of time.
title: Reading superconducting qubits while suppressing unwanted state transitions

description: Skeletal muscles, which are attached to bones and enable body movement, are crucial for metabolic regulation. "Sarcopenia," characterized by age-related declines in muscle mass and function, reduces mobility and severely undermines quality of life in old age. However, previous research has been constrained by substantial biological differences between animal models and humans, while conventional methods of culturing cells on flat (2D) dishes have remained ineffective in fully replicating the three-dimensional movements and contractile function of actual human muscles.
title: Team develops 3D biomimetic aging muscle model that can replace animal experiments

description: A researcher from Tokyo Metropolitan University has proposed a new interpretation of camouflage in nature. Most theories dismiss it as a form of communication because there is no apparent "signal" but rather a lack of one. Using an information-theoretic approach, the researcher shows that camouflage can be framed as an "information-masking" signal, one that disrupts the flow of information. The same idea might be applied to the wider field of communication, where signals may actively conceal information rather than convey it.
title: Is camouflage a form of communication?

description: Over the course of a year, hyperscale data centers (HDCs)—the largest and most powerful class of data centers, supporting services such as cloud computing, large language model training and global deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) tools—are powered mostly by fossil fuels and use as much electricity as entire U.S. states, according to a new study led by Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and the Harvard Data Science Initiative. The study provides one of the first facility-level estimates of HDCs' electricity use and carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions since the rise of AI.
title: U.S. hyperscale data centers' combined electricity use rivals that of some states

description: Researchers have resolved a long-standing paradox in polariton chemistry—a field that explores how to control chemical reactions by trapping molecules inside optical cavities where light and matter strongly interact (known as strong coupling). Previously, a major theoretical hurdle stood in the way: Calculations indicated that millions of inactive molecular states—known as dark modes—should greatly outnumber active polaritons, making it seemingly impossible for light-matter coupling to influence chemistry.
title: Quantifying dark modes to advance polariton chemistry

description: In a study published in Optical Fiber Technology, researchers from the Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed a new method to control multi-pulse generation in a 1972-nm mode-locked fiber laser. By applying external mechanical modulation to the optical fiber, the researchers generated multiple adjustable pulse patterns without increasing the pump power. This offers a simpler and more flexible approach to controlling ultrafast laser output.
title: New mechanical modulation method enables tunable multi-pulse fiber lasers

description: A new survey of the sky, from the largest structures in the universe to the dust and magnetic fields in our own Milky Way, is now fully underway. After two years of calibration, additional telescopes and a new solar array to provide energy security, the Simons Observatory (SO) in Chile's Atacama Desert is fully online and conducting science operations. Researchers at the Kavli Institute for Particle Astrophysics and Cosmology (KIPAC) at Stanford and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have had a hand in nearly every part of it.
title: Now fully online, the Simons Observatory will shape new studies of the Milky Way and the cosmos

description: Australian political parties are turning to AI "ensloppification" to win votes. We've seen One Nation post AI-generated, race-based Facebook clips attacking migration. Labor has shared a Halloween-themed reel using a cloned voice to claim Victorian Liberal leader Jess Wilson wants "Americanized" health care.
title: Five ways to spot AI misinformation before you vote

description: A potentially historic El Niño weather event could trigger far-reaching consequences for global food security and public health, according to researchers writing in the journal Nature.
title: Researchers warn that powerful El Niño could trigger global food and health crises

description: Lake trout are known for retreating into cold, deep water during summer. But beneath winter ice, some swim surprisingly close to the surface while others remain far below.
title: Where do fish go in the winter? Researchers listen beneath the ice to find out

description: Peekachu, Rain, Osiris, Caspian, Jellybean and Cyprus are dead. They were six of the 30 beluga whales removed from Marineland in Niagara Falls earlier this year. Echo is dead too. She was one of the four dolphins who were also removed around the same time. For all intents and purposes, she was blind.
title: Was a kinder fate possible for Marineland's animals? How the planning process failed them

description: Today, many leading quantum computers are built from superconducting circuits. However, the qubits in these circuits can easily lose energy to their surroundings, scrambling the fragile quantum information they hold.
title: Hidden defects return a qubit's lost energy

description: Children who receive a Steiner education show greater academic success in multiple subjects than those at mainstream schools, a new international study has found.
title: Steiner and state: Comparing two schools of thought

description: Artificial intelligence models are easy to pressure into giving out false climate information despite being initially reliable, finds a new UNESCO-UCL report to be launched at an international conference.
title: AI systems are easy to pressure into giving false climate information

description: When a massive outage hit Microsoft late last week, much of the digital world ground to a halt. The outage wiped out key Microsoft services including Outlook, Teams and Copilot, which are used by more than 430 million people around the world. As email and internal communications froze, the operations of governments and businesses went dark alongside them, triggering an economic paralysis that could cost billions of dollars.
title: Microsoft outage shows that big tech can't be treated as too big to fail

description: If you've ever been grounded at the airport due to thick fog, you'll understand the frustration this often overlooked weather phenomenon can cause.
title: Foggy days are becoming more common across southern Australia: New study

description: Globally, there have been concerns about the likelihood of artificial intelligence (AI) taking people's jobs and reducing job opportunities for college graduates.
title: AI is set to change the graduate job market. Here's how universities can respond

description: Over the past several decades, researchers have demonstrated quantum teleportation, the transfer of one quantum system's state to another, in a range of systems. However, many quantum computers encode logical qubits (units of quantum information) across groups of physical qubits, which makes teleporting the encoded state without losing information more challenging.
title: Quantum teleportation method uses weaker entanglement to transfer encoded information

description: A new study shows that many jurisdictions have fallen short of the foster care placement guidelines of the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978. The law requires that when a state takes an American Indian or Alaska Native (AIAN) child into foster care, the state must first seek to place that child with a family member, a member of the child's tribal nation or another Native family.
title: Foster care placement of American Indian and Alaska Native children falls short of federal legislation aims

description: Fuel breaks are linear strips of land along which vegetation is cleared or thinned—constructed along ridgelines, roads and other strategic places—to give firefighters a better chance to safely slow or steer a fire. Often described as "speed bumps" for wildfires, fuel breaks rarely stop fire spread on their own, but they do give crews critical anchor points for building firelines, setting backfires or safely applying water and retardant. They have been used since the 1960s across many landscapes.
title: Wildfire modeling helps managers decide where to build and maintain fuel breaks

description: The rise in the number of young people not in work, education or training (known as NEETs) in the U.K. is largely driven by poor mental and physical health, according to a new study led by University College London (UCL) academics.
title: Rise in young people out of work and education largely driven by ill health

description: A new era of genome research began in 2012 with the discovery that CRISPR/Cas9 could function as molecular scissors to cut specific DNA sequences. Over time, scientists harnessed CRISPR as a genome-editing tool, which held the promise of precise gene removal and addition for research purposes, targeted therapies for genetic diseases like cystic fibrosis or Huntington's, and a future where personalized treatments are the norm. But a major shortcoming has snagged that progress: CRISPR can make off-target edits to parts of the genome never meant to be touched.
title: New tool tracks unintended CRISPR edits and their effects in individual cells

description: A college senior who wants to clean up debris pollution in Earth's orbit and a student who has researched AI use in healthcare are among the 32 Americans named as 2027 Rhodes scholars.
title: 32 Americans named as Rhodes scholars have variety of interests, from space junk to art history

description: South Korean officials are scrambling to prevent cheating on a national college entrance exam as concerns grow that artificial intelligence and smart devices are making fraud harder to detect.
title: AI cheating fears spook South Korea ahead of high-stakes college entrance exam
